statement: All else equal, permanently raising the federal marginal tax rate on ordinary income by 1 percentage point for those in the top (i.e., currently 35%) tax bracket would increase federal tax revenue over the next 10 years.
assumed_favored_direction: raise the top marginal income tax rate
note: ATRA raised the top rate from 35% to 39.6% (larger than 1 pp); TCJA set 37%, still above 35%.

statement: Eliminating tax deductions for non-investment personal interest expenses (e.g., on mortgages), with reductions in personal tax rates that are both budget neutral and keep the burden of taxes by income group the same, would lead to more efficient financing decisions by individuals.
assumed_favored_direction: end the non-investment personal interest deduction (with neutral rate cuts)
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: TCJA capped the mortgage interest deduction ($750k) and suspended home-equity interest; it did not eliminate it.

statement: Reducing the deductibility of interest expenses for non-financial businesses to equalize the overall tax cost of debt and equity financing, while using the extra revenue to reduce personal and corporate tax rates in a budget neutral fashion that also keeps the burden of taxes the same, would lead to more efficient financing decisions by firms.
assumed_favored_direction: limit business interest deductibility, revenue-neutral rate cuts
note: TCJA sec. 13301 limited business interest to 30% of adjusted taxable income and cut the corporate rate, but not revenue- or burden-neutral and not equalizing debt and equity.

statement: A tax on the carbon content of fuels would be a less expensive way to reduce carbon-dioxide emissions than would a collection of policies such as “corporate average fuel economy” requirements for automobiles.
assumed_favored_direction: federal carbon price (tax or permit market)
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: No federal carbon tax or economy-wide permit market by 2021-12-20 or since.

statement: Bans on the short selling of financial securities, such as stocks and government bonds, lead to prices that are further, on average, from their fundamental values.
assumed_favored_direction: no bans on short selling
note: No short-sale ban since 2008; Rule 201 (2010) is a price test, not a ban. 'Adopted' = favored absence of a ban.

statement: Consumers would not necessarily be better off if cable and satellite TV firms were required to offer a la carte pricing for individual channels, because the networks' programming charges and the satellite-and-cable fees could adjust in response to this rule.
assumed_favored_direction: no a la carte requirement for cable and satellite
note: A la carte mandate bill introduced, never enacted. 'Adopted' = favored absence of the rule.

statement: Subjecting online sales from out-of-state vendors to the same retail sales taxes imposed on in-state sales would raise more tax revenue in the states making this change while reducing the pro-online bias of current policy.
assumed_favored_direction: tax out-of-state online sales like in-state sales
note: No federal law (Marketplace Fairness Act passed Senate only); states adopted the measure after South Dakota v. Wayfair, a court ruling, not a federal law, rule or executive measure.

statement: Taxpayers would be better protected if each money market fund in the U.S. were instead required to trade at its floating net asset value.
assumed_favored_direction: floating NAV for each money market fund
note: SEC 2014 rule: floating NAV only for institutional prime and institutional municipal funds; retail and government funds exempt.

statement: In the absence of floating net asset values, taxpayers would be better protected if each money market fund in the U.S. were required to set aside capital to protect against losses while holding back a portion of shareholders' cash for a time when they seek to withdraw all of their money.
assumed_favored_direction: capital buffer and redemption holdback for money market funds
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: SEC 2014 adopted liquidity fees and gates instead; no capital buffer or minimum balance at risk.

statement: Rules that tie each college's eligibility for federal student loans to its students' graduation rates and post-schooling employment outcomes would better protect taxpayers from losses on student loans.
assumed_favored_direction: tie federal student-loan eligibility to graduation and employment outcomes
note: 2014 gainful-employment rule (in force 2015-07-01 to 2019) tied eligibility of GE programs only to debt-to-earnings, not graduation rates; rescinded 2019-07-01; new GE/FVT rule 2023-10-10, effective 2024-07-01.

statement: The current trade barriers in the U.S. sugar industry raise the profits of sugar producers and make the typical U.S. consumer pay more for sugar and goods that use sugar as an input.
assumed_favored_direction: remove US sugar trade barriers
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: Sugar program and tariff-rate quotas continued in the 2018 farm bill.

statement: Ethanol content requirements and protectionism against imported ethanol (which includes fuel from sugarcane) raise food prices without significantly reducing carbon-dioxide emissions.
assumed_favored_direction: repeal the ethanol mandate and ethanol protection
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: Renewable Fuel Standard still in force; source date = date accessed.

statement: Consider the other of two proposals for restraining future Medicare spending, each by the same amount: The method that Governor Romney advocates — giving future seniors a fixed payment for premiums and letting private insurers compete with Medicare — imposes risks on future Medicare patients because competition may not be powerful to enough to offer future seniors the same quality of care that is currently promised without supplementing their premium support.
assumed_favored_direction: no Medicare premium support
note: Premium support passed the House only in budget resolutions; never enacted. 'Adopted' = favored absence.

statement: Because firms and inventors do not capture the full returns from research and development, the government would increase the average well-being of Americans (and potentially of others too) by favoring R&D using the tax code.
assumed_favored_direction: favor R&D in the tax code
note: Research credit (sec. 41) extended by ATRA 2013 and made permanent by the PATH Act 2015.

statement: Because all federal spending and taxes must be approved by both houses of Congress and the executive branch, a separate debt ceiling that has to be increased periodically creates unneeded uncertainty and can potentially lead to worse fiscal outcomes.
assumed_favored_direction: abolish the separate debt ceiling
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: Debt limit kept; suspended by the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023.

statement: The average US citizen would be better off if a larger number of highly educated foreign workers were legally allowed to immigrate to the US each year.
assumed_favored_direction: admit more highly educated immigrants
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: S.744 passed the Senate, not the House; H-1B cap and employment green-card numbers unchanged.

statement: Because the US has underspent on new projects, maintenance, or both, the federal government has an opportunity to increase average incomes by spending more on roads, railways, bridges and airports.
assumed_favored_direction: more federal infrastructure spending
note: IIJA within the window. Still in force: authorizations extended to 2026-12-11 (CRS R48845, https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R48845.html, 2026-09-02).

statement: Restricting US exports of liquefied natural gas would have adverse effects on the US economy.
assumed_favored_direction: do not restrict LNG exports
note: DOE approved non-FTA exports from 2014 on; a pause on new approvals ran 2024-01-26 to 2025-01-21, after which approvals resumed.

statement: An effective way to increase savings rates of employees whose firms have defined contribution plans is to combine automatic enrollment in those plans and periodic automatic increases in their contributions (with the ability to opt out of either).
assumed_favored_direction: automatic enrollment with automatic escalation in DC plans
note: PPA 2006 automatic-enrollment safe harbor (with escalation) in force throughout; SECURE 2.0 (2022-12-29) requires it for new plans from 2025.

statement: By lowering bargaining costs, fast-track negotiating authority for the president makes it more likely that the U.S. can conclude major trade deals.
assumed_favored_direction: fast-track (trade promotion) authority
note: TPA enacted 2015; expired 2021-07-01.

statement: Considering the costs of restricting free choice, and the share of people in the US who choose not to vaccinate their children for measles, the social benefit of mandating measles vaccines for all Americans (except those with compelling medical reasons) would exceed the social cost.
assumed_favored_direction: mandate measles vaccination for all Americans
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: No federal mandate; requirements are set by states. Source date = date accessed.

statement: By providing important measures of US economic performance — including employment, consumer prices, wages, job openings, time allocation in households, and productivity — the Bureau of Labor Statistics creates social benefits that exceed its annual cost of roughly $610 million.
assumed_favored_direction: maintain BLS funding
note: BLS funded throughout; FY2026 final $708.5M (+0.6%); requested cut not enacted. Source date: month of publication.

statement: The “Cadillac tax” on expensive employer-provided health insurance plans will reduce costly distortions in US health care if it is allowed to take effect as scheduled in 2018.
assumed_favored_direction: let the Cadillac tax take effect
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: Delayed, then repealed before taking effect.

statement: Allowing US-based employers to hire many more immigrants with advanced degrees in science or engineering would lower (at least temporarily) the premium earned by current American workers with similar degrees.
assumed_favored_direction: admit many more advanced-degree immigrants
cause_code: blocked by interests or veto players
note: As for 49.
